## Who this is for

Lab members who code but have never used Snakemake. You should be able to run
commands in a terminal, read a short Python function and know what a BAM file
is. You do not need cluster experience: day 1 runs entirely on your laptop
(macOS, Linux, or Windows through WSL2), and day 2 shows how the same pipeline
moves to SLURM.

We use Snakemake **8.27.1**, the version the lab's pipelines pin.

## What you build

Over the two days you write **RegPipe**, a small pipeline for regulatory
genomics. It aligns ChIP-seq and DNase-seq reads, filters them, calls peaks,
builds consensus peaks and coverage tracks, measures how many reads land in
peaks, and draws the *MYC* locus with plotgardener. Every module adds one idea
to it, and you can check your work against a finished copy at four stopping
points.

The finished RegPipe follows the same layout as the lab's three production
pipelines, so the last part of the course is reading those.

::: {.pipeline-cards}
::: {.course-pipeline}
**RegPipe** (this course)\
ChIP-seq and DNase-seq: align, filter, peaks, consensus, bigWigs, FRiP, a
locus figure. [Code](https://github.com/jpflores-13/snakemake-course/tree/main/course-pipeline)
:::

::: {}
**MicroCPipe**\
Micro-C from FASTQ to `.pairs`, `.mcool` and `.hic`, with a QC report.
[Field guide](field-guide/microcpipe.qmd)
:::

::: {}
**TTpipe**\
TT-seq processing and analysis: STAR alignment, strand-split tracks,
DESeq2. [Field guide](field-guide/ttpipe.qmd)
:::

::: {}
**ChromSimPipe**\
Cohesin loop-extrusion simulations compared with Hi-C, one GPU job per
shard. [Field guide](field-guide/chromsimpipe.qmd)
:::
:::

## The data

The course data are real, public reads from HCT116 colorectal cancer cells:
ENCODE ChIP-seq for CTCF and H3K27ac (each with its input control) and
DNase-seq, two biological replicates each, plus ENCODE's RAD21 peaks as a
reference set. To keep everything laptop-sized, we kept only the reads that
ENCODE's GRCh38 alignments place in a 5 Mb window, chr8:125,000,000-130,000,000.
That window holds *MYC* and the gene desert upstream of it, where the
colorectal cancer risk enhancers sit. Every step that made the subset is in
`data/prepare/`, and [`data/README.md`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/snakemake-course/blob/main/data/README.md)
lists each file's source.

## How to use this site

Each lesson exists in three forms, all made from one source file:

- **The page** (what you are reading now): the full text with every
  explanation, for working on your own or reading after the workshop.
- **The slides**: the same lesson as reveal.js slides, for the instructor and
  for following along in the room. Find them under *Also as: Slides* on each
  lesson page. Press `s` for speaker notes, `f` for full screen.
- **The answers**: every exercise links to a worked answer that explains
  *why*, not only *what*. The answer keys are public. Try the exercise first:
  most take five minutes, and the mistakes are where you learn.

If you fall behind, copy the folder of the last stopping point and carry on
from there. Nobody needs to finish every exercise to follow the next module.

After the lessons, the [field guide](field-guide/index.qmd) walks through the
lab's pipelines, the [Snakemake-ify exercise](exercises/snakemakeify.qmd)
turns a folder of shell scripts into a workflow, and the
[capstone](capstone.qmd) is a pipeline of your own. Keep the
[cheat sheet](cheatsheet.qmd) open while you work (it also prints on two
pages).
